decisions.minimum_change: Set the surprise's level_low/level_high to the home's own object (13.86, scale 0.01, evidence 'cents') and level_unit to usd, matching the DAL #157/#158 control where the metric home and its surprise carry the identical 64-cent level. RESIDUAL, stated not hidden: the sentence compares the GROWTH to the target while Rule 9.6 matches on the home's level, so the comparison's own subject is carried by the quote rather than by a value slot.

decisions.owning_clause: Served prefix :496 - 'A real slice is a business population for which "revenue/earnings from ___" makes sense. Accounting labels are not slices.' - and :497 - 'Omitted slice = consolidated whole-company (metric/guidance/surprise) or no-applicable-part (action).'
decisions.minimum_change: Empty slice_parts. 'Revenue from the March 2024 Share Repurchase Program' is not a business population; a board authorization is a filing-taxonomy label, and this is an ACTION fact, for which :497 expressly provides the no-applicable-part omission. My SEQ 2006 reasoning - that an unclear kind makes the unknown fallback its home - is withdrawn: the unknown kind is for a real company part whose KIND is unclear, never a licence to turn a non-business object into a part. Which program was revoked stays in the quote, which is where Rule 3.10 leaves it once numbers and filing-taxonomy labels are barred from the name. The complete law does not save the token either: the same block's 'unknown axis -> PROVISIONAL, never silently dropped' sentence governs how CODE maps an unfamiliar XBRL axis at runtime, and it sits AFTER :496's gate defining what a real slice is; it is not a producer licence to admit an object that fails that gate. Issue 53's Space NK facilities are NOT reopened.
